script: "Her brother's drunk guests stole my keys—now I am stuck, and I am terrified.". I walked into the lobby at 9 pm, the night shift was quiet except for the chatter of the baseball team's parents and the clatter of kids on the floor. My brother and sister, both around 35 and straight up trashed, sauntered in with beers in hand, looking like they'd just walked out of a bar fight. They wanted rooms, not a ride home, so I handed them keys after a quick, "How's the night?" joke. The rooms were in her name, so I had the dude scribble his name on the registration form. He looked like a 3‑year‑old; the last name ran off the edge, illegible, but who cared—he'd lost his wallet, no ID to prove anything. (Micro‑hook: "His handwriting looked like a toddler's ransom note.") At about 10:30 pm, the bartender closed up and told me the kids were playing baseball in the parking lot. I didn't know if they were still there, but the lot was already full, and the idea of a drunk truck‑driver circling those cars—maybe even the kids—made my stomach turn. "No, you can't drive," I said. "But I can park your truck for you." The truck was under the awning; the hotel had a rule that vehicles can't stay there long term because of emergency access. I was alone, the night shift, so I pulled up the truck. He nodded, "Sure, just grab another beer." He disappeared, came back with a new can, and plopped down on the sofa. I parked the truck, and when I returned, the dude was already in the lobby. The sister emerged from the elevator, clutching an ID and saying she didn't know her room number. Within fifteen minutes she'd lost her keys, looking like a drunk‑drunk version of me. I handed her new keys and left for the night. The next day, after I'd already started work, I went to the GM's office to explain what'd happened. She said, "Yeah, it was a bad decision. It's a huge liability for the hotel." I worked that Saturday and Sunday, then took two days off. When I came back today, she called me into her office and fired me on the spot. I just want to rant and ask what you all think of this situation. I am thinking wrongful termination—refusing to commit an illegal act, maybe. It's a mid‑size hotel across the US. (End.)
